newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU proposes initial 0.2% GDP fine on high deficits.
newsitem.headline: EU proposes initial 0.2% GDP fine on high deficits.

text.p: The European Commission has proposed an initial fine of 0.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) for EU members inside monetary union running excessive deficits, the Commission said on Wednesday.

The Commission also said in a document that an additional 0.1 percent of GDP would be levied as a fine for every percentage point by which a country exceeds the deficit/GDP ratio in the Maastricht Treaty on monetary union.
This ratio dictates that a member's budget deficit as a percentage of GDP must not exceed three percent.
The maximum fine would be 0.5 percent of GDP.
The Commission said such fines would not be imposed if a country were in a "severe recession". It did not define that economic condition.
These proposals will be discussed by European Finance Ministers in the coming weeks with a final agreement expected by the time of the summit of EU leaders in Dublin in December.
